text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Friday.

LONDON - The UK stock market ended the week on a firm note, buoyed by healthy gains on Wall Street and debt markets after U.S. producer price and retail sales data soothed worries about U.S. inflation and interest rates. The FTSE 100 share index, which spent much of the week defending the 4,000 level, ended at 4,028.1 up 33.4 points, a rise of 3.3 from October 4.

FRANKFURT- German shares closed bourse dealings slightly ahead after a session crippled by uncertainty before the release of U.S. inflation data. The 30-share DAX index ended up 5.28 points to 2,686.03, up 2.75 from Friday week. In post-bourse trade the DAX index stood at 2,692.69.

PARIS - French shares ended higher after key U.S. economic data showed inflation was restrained, but turnover remained limited as many investors had stayed on the sidelines awaiting the U.S. figures. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 11.49 points or 0.54 percent to 2,147.12, down 5.57 from seven days ago.

ZURICH - Swiss shares posted slight gains, edging above the psychologically important level of 3,800 points in the Swiss Market Index (SMI) after U.S. producer prices and retail sales data buoyed the market in late trade. "We had a very quiet day although the U.S. data were positive," a trader said. He added that fundamentals remained good but next week's trading may be shaky because several warrants on numerous blue-chip shares will expire on October 18. The All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) closed up 5.26 points or 0.22 percent to 2,435.79, up 3.88 from last Friday.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks closed moderately higher after drifting in a narrow range for most of the day, sandwiched by a national holiday on Thursday and the weekend, brokers expected the top to be capped next week, as the market lacked factors to stimulate fresh buying. The key 225-share Nikkei average rose 97.33 points or 0.47 percent to close at 20,968.16, falling 179.87 from last week.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks ended slightly easier as the market underwent some consolidation following its strong run up earlier in the week. "The market needs a period of consolidation," said William Choi, head of Hong Kong sales at SBC Warburg. The Hang Seng Index slipped 24.07 points to close at 12,218.40, rising 312.89 from last Friday.

SYDNEY - The Australian share market came near to setting a record closing high after major resource issues were buoyed by stronger metal prices. The key share market barometer, the All Ordinaries index, ended 13.3 points higher at 2,336.8, up 25.1 from seven days ago.

JOHANNESBURG - South African stocks closed up as positive sentiment returned to the market when Wall Street was reassured by potentially inflation-sensitive data and went on to post opening gains, U.S. retail sales and September producer prices confirmed moderate growth with inflation under control for the U.S. economy. The Dow strengthened and dispelled dealers' fears that it would correct and drag South African markets down with it. The All-share index ended up 23 points to 7,054.5, a rise of 33.9 from last week, as Industrials jumped 31.7 points to 8,270.4 up 48 from a week ago and the Gold index fell back 11.8 points to 1,728.2, down 5.6 from Friday week.
